reason: The case needs a structure, and folding the metal stock in the jig seems like a natural first step.
expectation: I expect to make a case shell or frame, though it will likely still need insulation and refrigeration.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the cold packs also seems useful, but I want to build the case first.

effect: The jig made a field case shell, giving me a structure to insulate.
reaction: The result was expected and straightforward.
reason: Adding insulation to the shell seems like the next practical step toward keeping the core cold.
expectation: I expect an insulated case shell that will still need refrigeration and cold packs.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the cold packs also seems necessary, but I want to finish the case structure first.

effect: The shell is now insulated and ready for the refrigeration insert.
reaction: The result was expected and straightforward.
reason: The refrigeration insert looks like the next part needed to keep the case cold.
expectation: I expect a refrigerated case, though it may still need the cold packs prepared separately.

alternatives.reason: The cold packs also need preparation, but I want to assemble the case first.

effect: The case now has refrigeration and a cradle for the core's liner; the radiator releases extracted heat to the air.
reaction: The explanation of where the heat goes was useful.
reason: Freezing the cold packs is the only available combination and seems necessary to prepare the case for the journey.
expectation: I expect the freezer to prepare the cold packs for use with the refrigerated case.

effect: The packs are ready to absorb heat during transfer, but need active refrigeration to restore their capacity.
reaction: The distinction between temporary heat absorption and refrigeration was useful.
reason: Combining the conditioned packs with the refrigerated case is the only available combination and should complete its cold storage setup.
expectation: I expect a prepared cold case for transporting the core, though it may need further preparation.

effect: The case is complete: refrigeration maintains its temperature, while the cold packs provide a short buffer during power changes.
reaction: The distinction between continuous cooling and a temporary backup made the finished case more understandable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the cold packs was most worthwhile because it explained that they absorb heat only for a limited time and need refrigeration to restore their capacity.

leastWorthwhile.text: Folding and insulating the case were predictable assembly steps, with little to consider beyond the obvious sequence.

surprise.text: The explanation that the refrigerator releases extracted heat through an exposed radiator clarified how the case moves heat away.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each part had a clear role, although the later choices were effectively forced.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see whether a whole piece of the band can be recovered and what it reveals, though this chapter itself was mostly straightforward assembly.
